segments: ... sent {OCR?} al-Mu'tasim for his bedding and his garments.
And in the year 1147 [AG, AD 836], [he sent an envoy] to the king of the Nabateans {OCR? Noba / Nubians}, that is the Nubians, to send tribute according to the ancient custom,
and if not, he would send an army against him.
And when the envoy arrived,
he found that the king of the Nubians had died,
and a young man named George,
who on his mother's side was descended from the royal line,
had arisen,
and his father Zacharias was governing.
Then that Zacharias, when he saw that the Arabs were strong, said to the envoy:
"In truth, there was an obligation upon us every year of 360
Moorish {OCR? Black/Nubian} slaves,
and apes {OCR? baboons/monkeys} that are trained and learn to imitate the actions of human beings,
and camelopards, that is giraffes,
and elephants' tusks, and leopards' skins.
However, the Arab kings also owed us an obligation of such-and-such an amount of kors of wheat, and choice garments,
and that we should have the one who collects the poll-tax from the Nubians who live in the land of the Arabs.
And when they broke off [their obligation],
we broke off [ours].
Nevertheless, because we have heard of the goodness of your king {OCR?} and the greatness of his lineage,
we will not conduct negotiations through an envoy,
but that our new king himself will come in person to do homage to him."
Then the envoy quickly sent word to inform al-Mu'tasim.
And he replied,
"Let him come."
And he ordered the governors of Egypt
to go out to meet him as far as Aswan, the border city.
And when he reached Fustat, they were to give him as many camels as sufficed for his retinue,
and thirty dinars every day for his expenses.
And thus that George was conducted in pomp through the lands of the Arabs.
For he was riding a camel with a saddle,
and above him was a canopy, a dome draped with purple {OCR? crimson?},
and a golden cross was fixed on top of it,
and in one hand he held a rod,
with Nubian youths walking on his right and on his left.
And a bishop also rode before him, holding the life-giving cross in his hands,
and horsemen and servants riding horses were around him.
And when he went down to Baghdad and paraded through the streets,
he lodged in one of the royal palaces.
Then a Nubian man, who had been collecting the tribute of the Nubians in the land of the Arabs and had rebelled against the king of the Nubians and converted to Islam, slandered George, saying:
"This man is not the son of the king,
but an impostor."
